hypotheses.text: The onset of sensory deficits in FDXR deficiency follows an ocular-first progression: visual failure due to optic atrophy and rod-cone retinal dystrophy manifests in early infancy or childhood (median age < 5 years), whereas auditory neuropathy spectrum disorder (HP:0000407) manifests significantly later, during late childhood or adolescence (median age >= 10 years).
hypotheses.rationale: Clarifying the temporal order of sensory organ failure is crucial for pediatricians: if optic atrophy and retinal dystrophy systematically precede auditory neuropathy, children presenting with unexplained early-onset optic atrophy or congenital amaurosis warrant proactive auditory brainstem response (ABR) surveillance even before overt hearing impairment appears.

evidence.text: In a cohort of Chinese Han patients with non-isolated auditory neuropathy, hearing loss onset ranged from 2 to 25 years with a mean onset age of 11 years, while systemic and visual manifestations often coexisted.

source.title: Identification of genetic mechanisms of non-isolated auditory neuropathy with various phenotypes in Chinese families
source.quote: Patients' age of hearing loss onset ranged from 2 to 25 years, averaging 11 years.

evidence.text: In 11 unrelated patients with biallelic FDXR variants ascertained for eye disease, four presented with nystagmus a few months after birth (diagnosed as congenital amaurosis) and seven presented in early childhood with nyctalopia and poor vision (diagnosed as early-onset severe retinal dystrophy).

source.title: FDXR-Associated Oculopathy: Congenital Amaurosis and Early-Onset Severe Retinal Dystrophy as Common Presenting Features in a Chinese Population
source.quote: Before the detection of FDXR variants, four patients were clinically diagnosed as congenital amaurosis due to the presence of nystagmus a few months after birth, while seven were diagnosed as early-onset severe retinal dystrophy due to the presence of nyctalopia and/or poor vision in early childhood.

numbers.metric: Patients presenting in early infancy or childhood with congenital amaurosis or early-onset retinal dystrophy

hypotheses.text: A subset of juvenile- or adult-onset FDXR deficiency (MMDS9B) cases present primarily with an acute or subacute sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy (HP:0009830) and gait ataxia (HP:0002066) that mimics Guillain-Barré syndrome or CIDP, preceding the clinical onset or diagnosis of core optic-acoustic manifestations.
hypotheses.rationale: Mitochondrial disorders are rarely considered when a patient presents with an acute motor-sensory neuropathy resembling an inflammatory demyelinating process; testing this hypothesis confirms whether FDXR should be in the differential diagnosis of atypical non-remitting acute polyneuropathies.

evidence.text: A literature review of 44 published FDXR cases showed peripheral polyneuropathy in 22.72% (10/44) and ataxia in 43.18% (19/44), with two newly identified siblings presenting with an acute/sub-acute onset of peripheral neuropathy mimicking acute inflammatory neuropathy before later manifesting classic optic and auditory signs.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease: a challenging differential diagnosis
source.quote: The review of clinical findings in previously described cases from literature reveals also a significant incidence of sensorimotor peripheral polyneuropathy (22.72%) and ataxia (43.18%)... Both patients presented with an acute-sub-acute onset of peripheral neuropathy and only in later stages of the disease developed the typical features of FDXR-associated disease.

hypotheses.text: Electroretinography (ERG) reveals severe, early-onset combined rod and cone photoreceptor dysfunction in 100% of FDXR-affected individuals presenting with vision loss, reliably differentiating FDXR deficiency from isolated primary mitochondrial optic neuropathies (LHON and OPA1-DOA) where photopic and scotopic ERG waveforms remain intact.
hypotheses.rationale: LHON and OPA1 typically affect retinal ganglion cells with preservation of photoreceptors, yielding normal full-field ERGs. Proving that rod-cone ERG impairment is an obligate feature of FDXR oculopathy provides a non-invasive, objective functional biomarker separating FDXR deficiency from pure optic atrophies.

evidence.text: All five evaluated patients with biallelic FDXR variants exhibited retinal dystrophy alongside optic atrophy, with ERG showing severely impaired cone and rod functions within their first decade of life.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort: Unraveling expanded ocular phenotypes and genetic spectrum
source.quote: all patients presented with retinal dystrophy, and electroretinogram showed severely impaired cone and rod functions in their first decades.

numbers.metric: Impaired cone and rod ERG in evaluated cohort

evidence.text: Fundus fluorescein angiography in 3 of 5 patients revealed severe retinal vascular abnormalities including delayed filling, complete occlusion, and peripheral nonperfusion, accompanying generalized retinal degeneration.

source.title: FDXR-associated disease in a Chinese cohort: Unraveling expanded ocular phenotypes and genetic spectrum
source.quote: Three of the five patients showed attenuated retinal vessels that appeared as white lines on the fundus, and fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA) further revealed vascular abnormalities including delayed filling, completely occluded retinal vasculature, and severe retinal vascular nonperfusion of the peripheral retina.

numbers.metric: Patients showing white-line attenuated retinal vessels and FFA occlusive changes

new_directions.question_text: What is the precise onset age distribution and longitudinal co-occurrence rate of optic atrophy versus auditory neuropathy in non-ocularly ascertained cohorts across all published FDXR patients?
new_directions.rationale: Ascertainment bias currently skews eye cohorts toward 100% retinal dystrophy and audiology cohorts toward hearing loss. Collating unbiased, multi-system systematic reviews will determine whether isolated auditory neuropathy ever truly persists without subclinical retinal degeneration.

new_directions.question_text: Can peripheral nerve electrophysiology (axonal vs. demyelinating polyneuropathy) discriminate FDXR deficiency from Charcot-Marie-Tooth type 2A and other mitochondrial neuropathies like MFN2?
new_directions.rationale: Masnada et al. observed that acute/subacute polyneuropathy can be the initial sign in over 20% of cases. Understanding the specific neurophysiological profile of FDXR neuropathy will aid early detection before sensory loss.
